analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The visible text units are base-side excerpts (lines 802-1610). The changed head ranges are 810-813, 829 and 1896-1899, and the patch excerpt is truncated.

The documented behavioral change is in GLM5Next video handling. Variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks are now indexed, not refused with a deterministic 400. Frame i is timed at i / nominalFrameRate, as in the reference loader. Separately, a new documentation bullet lists admitted inline video data-URI labels (`MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders`); its text is cut off in the supplied excerpt.

Security relevance:
- T-050 (inline video plaintext in provider temp files) and TB-007 (inference engine) bear on the video processing path. VFR acceptance widens which inputs reach AVFoundation decode. The documented bounds still apply: 512 MiB decoded-frame cap, 28,532-token pixel cap, VisionMemoryGate reservation, 600 s maximum duration, and the 25 MiB media cap.
- A VFR track with a wrong average rate could produce skewed timestamps. That affects correctness rather than confidentiality. Frame-count and decoded-bytes bounds were not shown to depend on constant frame rate.
- The docs state that media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture, so the T-041 cache channel is not widened.

No code is in scope here, so I verified no implementation. I could not confirm that `GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset` enforces the decoded-frame cap before any unbounded allocation on VFR tracks with very high frame counts. I also could not see the full inline-video-label bullet, including whether the label only gates the path and does not skip sniffing or validation. That should be checked against the source change in a code-bearing pass. I report no findings from documentation alone.
